text:
kai: Quick follow-up from last week's postmortem: two similar regressions during incremental releases. We need concrete guardrails for releases, owners, and timelines.

mira: Agreed. Can you propose thresholds and an action plan? Keep defaults conservative.

sam: Proposal: initial canary 0.5% traffic, second 2%, third 8%. Auto-rollback if error_rate >= baseline +5pp for 3m OR p95_latency >= baseline +200ms for 2m. Also block release if schema errors >0.2% in smoke test. Max canary blast radius 3%.

kai: draft rollout policy snippet below, will attach to INF-5109 and create PRs.

```yaml
rollout_policy: incremental_guardrails
initial_batch: 0.5%
progression: [2%, 8%]
max_blast_radius: 3%
rollback_triggers:
  - id: error_spike
    metric: error_rate
    threshold: +0.05
    evaluation_window: 3m
  - id: latency_jump
    metric: p95_latency
    threshold_ms: +200
    evaluation_window: 2m
smoke_test:
  schema_error_threshold: 0.002
  run_after_each_batch: true
auto_rollback: true
```

jena: Added INF-5109 tracking card. Owners suggested: sam -> rollback implementation + smoke tests; kai -> rollout config + infra deploy; mira -> metrics/dashboards + runbook. Deadlines: smoke tests by Tue EOD, infra review Wed AM, staged rollouts Thu.

sam: I'll implement the rule engine hooks and add synthetic payloads to the smoke harness. PR ETA Tue.

mira: I'll make a focused runbook section for on-call: signal interpretation, manual abort, and whom to page. Pager for sev2+, slack for sev3.

deploy-bot: Canary plan queued by @kai: incremental-guardrails/v1 scheduled for 2026-05-10 02:00 UTC.

kai: Also adding pre-rollout checklist: verify tokenizer/codec compatibility for models, confirm no model swap during rollout, run model-diff on canary slice. Last 3 incidents had model-swap + tokenizer mismatch pattern.

sam: I'll add circuit-breaker tagging so canary traffic is isolated and can't cascade.

jena: Created recurring "Release Guardrails Review" monthly. We'll revisit thresholds and incident trends.

mira: Once INF-5109 has PR links and runbook, we can consider gradually tightening defaults. For now keep defaults strict. :thumbsup:
